title: Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Measurement by Telemetry
author: Lynette Bower
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yevfte6
materials: Loosely tape the animal’s forelimbs to the table.
Maintain supplemental warmth throughout the anesthetic recovery.
The analgesic Buprenex is administered post-surgically.

steps.title: Surgical Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the animal for surgery using anesthesia and sterile technique.

substeps.instruction: Administer an appropriate concentration of Isoflurane anesthesia to achieve a deep anesthetic plane; maintain throughout the procedure.
Shave body hair from all intended incision sites.
Surgically scrub the incision sites.
Establish a sterile field.

steps.title: Animal Positioning and Initial Incision
steps.instruction: Position the animal and create the initial surgical access to the neck.

substeps.instruction: Position the animal in dorsal recumbency on the surgery table with the head closest to the surgeon.
Provide supplemental warmth during the surgery.
Loosely tape the animal's forelimbs to the table.
Apply sterile draping material to the sterile surgical field.
Make a 1.5 cm midline incision through the skin on the neck using small surgical scissors.
Maintain tissue hydration throughout the procedure by irrigating tissues with saline (0.9% sodium chloride) as needed.

steps.title: Isolate the Carotid Artery
steps.instruction: Expose and isolate the left carotid artery from surrounding tissues.

substeps.instruction: Separate the mandibular glands using sterile cotton tip applicators.
Retract the left mandibular gland using an elastic stay hook and tape the hook to the surgery table.
Locate the carotid artery along the left side of the trachea using sterile cotton tip applicators.
Isolate the vessel from surrounding tissue using fine tipped, curved forceps, ensuring the vagus nerve is not disturbed.

steps.title: Prepare Artery for Cannulation
steps.instruction: Place sutures to ligate, occlude, and secure the carotid artery.

substeps.instruction: Pass three pieces of 5-0 or 6-0 non-absorbable suture under the isolated artery section.
Position the ligation suture just proximal to the bifurcation of the interior and exterior carotid arteries; tie a secure knot and tape the tails to the table.
Position the occlusion suture (closest to the heart) and the middle suture as close to the clavicle as possible, isolating at least 6 mm of the artery; tie loose knots in both.
Clamp a hemostat on one of the tails of the middle suture.

steps.title: Prepare the Transmitter and Introducer
steps.instruction: Prepare the telemetry device and the needle introducer for implantation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the transmitter from the sterile package to the sterile field, avoiding grasping the catheter to prevent damage to the sensor.
Turn the AM radio on and remove the tip cover by alternating gentle traction and release to prevent gel loss.
Examine the catheter under high magnification for bubbles or gel loss; re-gel if necessary.
Prepare a catheter introducer by bending the beveled tip of a 25-gauge syringe needle downward to approximately 90° using a needle holder (beveled side facing up).
Optionally place the needle onto a 1 cc syringe to serve as a handle.

steps.title: Cannulate the Carotid Artery
steps.instruction: Insert the catheter into the artery and position it in the aortic arch.

substeps.instruction: Gently apply tension to the occlusion suture (closest to the clavicle) using a hemostat to elevate and occlude the artery.
Grasp the catheter tip just distal to the thin-walled section using Vessel Cannulation Forceps.
Pierce the artery just proximal to the ligation suture using the 25-gauge needle introducer and insert the catheter upstream toward the aorta.
Withdraw the catheter introducer.
Advance the catheter into the artery until it reaches the occlusion suture.
Position the middle suture around the artery and catheter, then tighten the knot to secure the catheter.
Release tension on the occlusion suture and advance the catheter beyond the suture into the thoracic cavity.
Continue advancing until at least 2 mm of the sensing region is positioned in the aortic arch.

steps.title: Secure the Catheter
steps.instruction: Seal the artery and anchor the catheter in place.

substeps.instruction: Tighten the occlusion suture and the middle suture around the artery and catheter to seal the artery wall around the catheter stem.
Release tension on the ligation suture and tie the loose ends around the catheter stem to anchor it.
Trim all suture tails as short as possible.
Optionally apply a very small drop of Vetbond tissue adhesive to the suture knots using a gel-loading micropipette tip.

steps.title: Place the Subcutaneous Device
steps.instruction: Create a pocket and implant the transmitter.

substeps.instruction: Use small surgical scissors to form a subcutaneous pocket via blunt dissection (ensure it is large enough to prevent pressure necrosis).
Irrigate the pocket with a 3 cc syringe filled with warm, sterile saline; ensure the syringe slides the full length of the pocket.
Insert the HD-X11 transmitter against the body.
Secure the transmitter in place using a small drop of Vetbond tissue adhesive dispensed from a 1 cc syringe (needle removed).
Secure the catheter to surrounding tissue using small drops of Vetbond tissue adhesive via a gel-loading micropipette tip.

steps.title: Prepare ECG Leads
steps.instruction: Modify the transmitter leads for electrode placement.

substeps.instruction: Shorten lead material to the appropriate length with scissors, coiling a small amount under the skin for animal growth.
Use a sharp sterile scalpel blade to cut the silicone tubing at the tip of the lead and remove approximately 1 cm to expose the stainless steel wire.
Create tip covers by pulling the excess silicone tubing to the end of the lead and securing it with 5-0 or 6-0 non-absorbable suture.
Place another suture around the silicone tubing just proximal to the exposed wire to inhibit fluid migration.
Repeat these steps for each lead.

steps.title: Position and Secure ECG Leads
steps.instruction: Tunnel the leads to the target muscle regions and secure them.

substeps.instruction: Grasp the positive lead (red tubing) with a small hemostat and tunnel it subcutaneously from the neck incision to the left caudal rib region (approximately 1 cm left of the xyphoid process).
Grasp the negative lead (clear tubing) with a small hemostat and tunnel it subcutaneously from the neck incision to the right pectoral muscle.
Ensure both leads lie flat against the muscle to avoid tissue irritation.
Secure both leads near the neck incision by placing a stay suture through the chest muscle and around the leads using 5-0 or 6-0 non-absorbable suture.

steps.title: Close Incision and Recovery
steps.instruction: Close the surgical site and manage post-operative recovery.

substeps.instruction: Close the skin incision using 5-0 or 6-0 absorbable or non-absorbable suture.
Seal the incision with Vetbond tissue adhesive.
Discontinue surgical anesthesia.
Maintain supplemental warmth throughout anesthetic recovery.
Administer the analgesic Buprenex post-surgically.
Monitor the animal closely for the return of normal postures and behaviors.
